Rival Hero Academies.text: U.A. Academy is the most famous hero academy in Japan, not the only one. People speak of U.A. in the east and Shiketsu Academy in the west. Shiketsu is nearly as hard to enter, drills formal courtesy into students who wear dark uniforms with peaked caps, and trains rescue, teamwork and public conduct as hard as combat, on the principle that a hero's image is part of the job. Ketsubutsu Academy, whose hero course counts Ms. Joke, the Smile Hero, among its teachers, has a reputation for friendly manners off the field and shrewd, calculated play once a contest starts. Seiai Academy and smaller academies across the country complete the field. All of them follow U.A.'s pattern: three-year programs for high-school graduates, each with its own campus, uniform, rules and traditions. Their students meet U.A.'s at the Provisional Hero License Exam, the Commission's licensing test, and at occasional joint events. They never enter U.A.'s Sports Festival, which belongs to U.A. alone, but many watch its broadcast to scout future rivals and build strategies around the Quirks they see on television. The academies compete every winter for the best applicants, and a strong applicant may sit more than one entrance exam. Between academies the rivalry is mostly pride: Shiketsu students measure themselves against U.A. at every chance, and U.A. students learn quickly that a polite stranger from another academy may already know their Quirk. Until they hold a license, students of every academy are bound by the same Quirk law as everyone else.
